anchor.note: feet / ground point of the character, in pixels from the frame's top-left

camera.note: one tile on the ground is pixelsPerTile wide and pixelsPerTile*sin(elevation) tall on screen

sheetLayout: rows = directions (in the order above), columns = frames, no padding

groundMotion.note: planted feet stay still when fps = speed (tiles/s) * fpsPerTilePerSec; at the design speed that is the fps above

tintGuidance.mode: multiply (Phaser setTint); untinted layers are drawn as they are
tintGuidance.belt: the profile's belt.color; a dark (black) belt.color is drawn as #26272f
tintGuidance.belt-center: two-colour belts only: belt.color2; a dark (black) color2 is drawn as deep black #111116 (it sits between two coloured bands, not next to the outline)
tintGuidance.belt-tape1 / belt-tape2: tape colour: #f4f1ea on dark belts, #1a1a1a on light belts (rule in apps/client/src/ui/belt.ts)
tintGuidance.belt-tape1-edge / belt-tape2-edge: no tint; draw each with its stripe (stripes >= 1 / >= 2)
tintGuidance.belt-sheen: dark (black) belt.color only: tint #a2a6b6, a bright top edge so black reads as a belt, not as outline; skip on other belts
tintGuidance.belt-center-edge: optional separator around the centre stripe; NOT used in the chosen style (skip it). Tint #ece6d8 if a future style wants it
tintGuidance.belt-rim: ALWAYS draw it, after belt-center: tint #2e2a3a (dark rim) on every belt except a dark (black) belt.color, which gets light #c9ccd6
tintGuidance.skin: multiply by a palettes.skin colour (the layer is a light neutral grey)
tintGuidance.hair: multiply every hair-* layer by a palettes.hair colour (light neutral grey)

beltStyles.note: chosen belt style (belt revision, option C): tint per layer for each Action Zone belt (fixtures/); a layer that is not listed is not drawn (belt-center-edge is never drawn in this style). Tape stripes keep the belt.ts rule

palettes.note: Recommended swatches (hex), shown by the game in this order. They are multiply tints for the tinted layers (skin, hair-*, gi). Skin runs from light to deep. The ids in palettesDraftLabels are placeholders for the Content Writer, not names

groups.note: draw exactly one layer of each group, after the base layers (face, then hair)

optionNotes.face-01: the approved face of Batch 1: oval eyes with a shine, friendly brows, a small smile
optionNotes.face-02: big round eyes, soft high brows, a wider smile
optionNotes.face-03: calm almond eyes, straight brows, a small smile
optionNotes.face-04: oval eyes with small lashes at the outer corner, a happy smile
optionNotes.face-05: bold thick brows, determined but friendly
optionNotes.face-06: oval eyes and freckles across the cheeks
optionNotes.hair-01: very short (close crop): a thin cap that follows the head
optionNotes.hair-02: short: the approved Batch 1 hair (cap, back, sideburns, a short fringe and a tuft)
optionNotes.hair-03: curly: a rounder cap made of soft curls
optionNotes.hair-04: afro: a rounded shape built from soft coil clumps with light tops, a natural hairline above the brows
optionNotes.hair-05: braids: a smooth cap with two braids hanging behind the ears to the shoulders
optionNotes.hair-06: ponytail: cap pulled back to a tie at the back of the head, a short tail (above the belt)
optionNotes.hair-07: bun: cap with a round bun on top towards the back
optionNotes.hair-08: tied back: smooth hair combed back to a low knot at the nape
optionNotes.hair-09: two puffs: hair parted down the middle and gathered into two round coil puffs high on the head
optionNotes.hair-10: short twists: a soft cap covered in short, rounded twists that point up and out (they never reach the eyes)
optionNotes.hair-11: cornrows into braids: neat raised rows from the hairline to the back, ending in braids that hang behind the shoulders
optionNotes.hair-12: high-top fade: short faded sides and a tall rounded flat-top of tight coils
